work_summary: Next.js security upgrade in progress on branch chore/next-16-4-3-cve (uncommitted). next 16.1.1 -> 16.4.3 clears 4 critical advisories to 0 critical (3 were Next.js: Image Optimizer DoS, RSC deserialization DoS, request smuggling in rewrites). tsc and next build both pass (68s). But the upgrade pulls eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1, which adds react-hooks/set-state-in-effect at error severity and flags 54 pre-existing sites across 42 files. Pinning eslint-config-next back to 16.1.1 does NOT help - the plugin resolves via ^7.0.0 regardless (verified: still 54 errors). Probed the rule against the installed plugin with 12 synthetic shapes; only effect-local async fn with a cancellation guard plus a reloadKey refetch (probe N) passes while preserving behaviour. Rejected the await-Promise.resolve() trick (probe J) on principle. Also probed: useCallback fetchers, useEffectEvent, plain async fns in component body, and moving setLoading to the handler all FAIL. Wrote a PRD and PRP plan splitting the work into Phase 1 (9 files, 12 errors, fetchers with a single call site) and Phase 2 (33 files, 42 errors, fetchers reused by buttons/pagination/post-save, in three groups by reuse count). Test coverage of the affected surface is thin: only 7 of the 42 files have a colocated test. Both docs are uncommitted: .claude/PRPs/prds/2026-11-01-next-16-4-3-react-hooks-rule.prd.md and .claude/PRPs/plans/2026-11-01-next-16-4-3-react-hooks-rule.plan.md. Two independent reviewers (sonnet + opus) were dispatched for /prp-validate-plan and were still running after 25 minutes when this handoff was written - their verdicts are NOT yet collected, so the plan is unvalidated.

WHY THE UPGRADE: npm audit --omit=dev went 4 critical -> 0 critical; the 3 Next.js ones were GHSA-9g9p-9gw9-jx7f (Image Optimizer DoS via remotePatterns), GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf (RSC deserialization DoS) and GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8 (request smuggling in rewrites). The app ships /api/v1 rewrites in next.config.js so the smuggling class is directly relevant. THE BLOCKER: next 16.4.3 pulls eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1 through eslint-config-next's range ^7.0.0. 7.1.1 turns on react-hooks/set-state-in-effect at the recommended preset, as an error. It flags 54 pre-existing sites in 42 files. TRAP: pinning eslint-config-next back to 16.1.1 does NOT remove them - the plugin resolves to 7.1.1 anyway. Verified by running lint with that mix: still 54 errors. WHAT THE RULE ACCEPTS (probed against the installed plugin with a throwaway flat config; the probe files were deleted, re-create them if needed): FAIL - setState directly in effect; useCallback fetcher with setState after await; plain async fn declared in the component body; useEffectEvent wrapper; moving setLoading into the click handler. PASS - async fn declared INSIDE the effect body with a cancellation guard, plus a reloadKey counter for refetch (this is the approved shape, 'probe N'); also passes are setState only inside a nested async / .then in the effect body, and await Promise.resolve() as the fetcher's first line. That last one is REJECTED on principle - it defeats the linter rather than fixing anything. SCOPE SPLIT (measured, not guessed): Phase 1 = 9 files / 12 errors, where the fetcher has a single call site. Phase 2 = 33 files / 42 errors, in three groups by fetcher reuse count; the heavy ones are app/admin/files/page.tsx (5 fetchers), lib/booking/store.ts (loadSlots 7 refs, under the LIFF booking flow) and components/admin/WalkinBookingDialog.tsx. One of the 54 is NOT this rule: app/liff/service-request/page.tsx:75 is react-hooks/immutability - a real use-before-declare ordering defect, fix it separately. TEST COVERAGE IS THIN: only 7 of the 42 files have a colocated test (admin/bookings, admin/requests, admin/rich-menus list|new|edit, liff/debt-mediation, components/ui/CalendarPickerTH). The other 35 rest on tsc + lint + build + Playwright smoke, which does not exercise admin CRUD. The plan forbids modifying test files - they are the contract. UNRESOLVED WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN: the two /prp-validate-plan reviewers (sonnet + opus) had been running 25+ minutes with no verdicts collected. The PRD and plan are therefore UNVALIDATED. Do not treat the plan as approved. If the reviewer output is gone, re-run /prp-validate-plan rather than inventing a verdict.
